insight.insight: A latent's sensitivity to a perturbation does not show what it represents. EEG power falls off as 1/f, so an alpha band-stop deletes far more signal energy than an equal-width sham notch. The raw alpha response therefore has to be checked against how much distortion each intervention causes, and against clean, unperturbed data, before a latent can be called an alpha feature. This reasoning yields a forked validation ladder: stages for sensitivity, distortion-controlled selectivity, specificity, and clean-data validation support a representational claim, while a separate readout-intervention stage supports a claim of task relevance.
dependent_results: Raw alpha/sham |Δf| ratio is 7.33 (95% CI [6.18,8.68]) and exceeds 1 in 27/27 settings. Normalized per unit time-domain distortion it falls to 1.32 ([1.12,1.55], 17/27). Normalized per unit removed spectral energy it falls to 0.28 ([0.22,0.36], 0/27) (Section 3.1, Table 2).
Code-overlap ratios follow the same pattern: raw 2.77, then 0.51 and 0.11 after normalization (Section 3.1).
Alpha is the maximum-|Δf| / minimum-Jaccard band in only 15/27 settings of the six-band sweep, a plurality rather than a rule (Section 3.1).
Alpha selectivity correlates only weakly with readout importance: mean r=0.107 (CI [0.068,0.146]) across 21 settings, with |r|≤0.32 in all nine BCI-middle retrainings (Section 3.2).

Zeroing specialist-like groups changes frozen-probe balanced accuracy by +0.0055 (CI [-0.007,0.027]), compared with -0.028 for fragile groups and -0.019 for random groups. Specialists are therefore not preferentially important to the linear readout (Section 3.2).

On clean EEG, specialists' signed r with relative alpha power is -0.073 (negative in 23/27 settings). Their mean |r| is 0.143, versus 0.246 for fragile latents and 0.097 for random latents. Among top-activating trials, specialists show only +0.012 more relative alpha power than matched fragile exemplars (Section 3.3).

Against activity-matched controls (firing 0.374 vs 0.374), specialists keep a small |r| edge (0.143 vs 0.101, Δ|r| CI [0.032,0.052], 27/27 settings), but the sign does not reverse. No alpha-representing latent is supported (Section 3.3, Appendix E).
Conclusion: the 7.3× signature fails the distortion control, does not mark latents that track clean alpha in the intended direction, and does not identify units the readout depends on (Section 5).
key_definitions: Setting: one combination of backbone (CBraMod, REVE, DINOv3), dataset (BCI, MA, Speech), and depth (early, middle, late), giving 27 in total (Section 2, Backbones and data).
TopK SAE: c=ReLU(TopK_k((x−b_dec)W_enc+b_enc)), x̂=cW_dec+b_dec, with k=32, trained with MSE plus AuxK (Section 2, TopK SAEs).
Alpha vs sham test: an 8–12 Hz band-stop compared with a width-matched 30–34 Hz notch, both fourth-order zero-phase Butterworth filters (Section 2, Perturbations).
Response metrics: sparse-code cosine, active-set Jaccard, and per-latent |Δf_j| (Section 2, Perturbations).

Distortion control: the SAE response divided either by time-domain ‖x−x̃‖₂/‖x‖₂ or by the fraction of spectral energy removed. Removed-energy ratios are 57.2/34.6/11.8 on BCI/MA/Speech (Section 2, Perturbations).
Specialist-like alpha latent: in the top quartile of alpha selectivity and at or below median channel-dropout fragility (Section 2, Selectivity).

Controls: size-matched general-fragile and random groups for readout tests; activity-matched non-specialists (nearest in clean firing rate and mean activation) for clean-alpha tests (Section 2; Appendix A).

Importance: |w_j|·E_train[c_j] from logistic probes on mean-pooled codes. Group ablation zeroes a selected set of codes and measures the change in balanced accuracy, either with a frozen probe or a retrained one (Section 2).
Independent observational validation: correlation of a latent's clean activation with trial-wise relative alpha power, a quantity not used in selection (Section 2).

Validation ladder: Stages 1–3 test sensitivity, distortion-controlled selectivity, and specificity. Stage 5 (observational validation) completes the representational claim. Stage 4 (readout intervention) is required only for a task-relevance claim (Section 1, Table 1, Figure 1).
Bootstrap CIs: 10,000 resamples over settings, not over latents (Section 2).
reasoning_steps: Observe a large raw alpha-over-sham response that is consistent across all settings, the tempting basis for an 'alpha feature' label (Section 3.1).
Note that the 1/f EEG spectrum makes the alpha notch remove far more energy than the sham, so the comparison confounds band identity with distortion magnitude (Section 2, Perturbations).

Normalize by distortion. The ratio drops to 1.32 with the time-domain denominator and to 0.28 with the spectral-energy denominator. The two denominators bracket the confound and show the response is not distortion-independent (Section 3.1).
Separate selection from evaluation: choose latents using perturbation responses, then evaluate them on clean data with a quantity not used in selection, to avoid circularity (Section 1; Section 2).
Clean-data validation shows negative signed correlation with relative alpha, so the latents do not fire on high-alpha trials as an alpha-detector reading would predict (Section 3.3).
Activity matching rules out the explanation that the fragile group's |r| advantage, or the specialists' own pattern, reflects baseline firing. The sign stays negative (Section 3.3).

Test task relevance separately: weak selectivity–importance correlation and null specialist ablations show the latents are not preferentially used by the readout. Under the ladder's fork, this is not required for a representational claim (Section 3.2; Figure 1).
Conclude that no stage beyond sensitivity is passed. A perturbation response alone does not justify a semantic name, and labels should match the evidence stage in Table 1 (Sections 4–5).
